case_name: Anuj Kumar Gupta @ Sethi Gupta v State of Bihar
respondent:
State of Bihar
Supreme Court of India

24 July 2013
Cr.A. No. 1575 of 2009
The Judgment was delivered by : Fakkir Mohamed Ibrahim Kalifulla, J.
1. This appeal is directed against the judgment of the High Court of Patna at Bihar dated 02.11.2007, passed in Criminal Appeal No.690 of 2005. The said appeal was disposed of along with Criminal Appeal No.606/2005, as well as Death Reference No.8 of 2005.
2. To trace the brief facts, the deceased Chhotu Kumar Das @ Abhinav Das (hereinafter referred to as 'Chhotu') son of the informant Gopal Prasad Das (PW-6), left his house on 21.04.2002 at about 8.15 p.m., for visiting a local Mela, which was held every year in the village on the eve of Ram Navami. Thereafter, he could not be traced inspite of a search by his parents and, therefore, a written report was submitted by PW-6 at the police station on 22.04.2002 at 10.30 a.m. briefly narrating the circumstances in which the deceased could not be traced. No suspicion
facts: The deceased Chhotu Kumar Das @ Abhinav Das left his house on 21.04.2002 at about 8.15 p.m., for visiting a local Mela, which was held every year in the village on the eve of Ram Navami.
Thereafter, he could not be traced inspite of a search by his parents and, therefore, a written report was submitted by PW-6 at the police station on 22.04.2002 at 10.30 a.m.
The investigation was carried out by PW-9, the Sub-Inspector of Police.
In the course of the investigation, he came across some suspicious materials against the appellant by some of the witnesses.
PW-9, therefore, interrogated the appellant on 22.04.2002, whereafter he was arrested.
issues: Whether the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant is liable to be set aside?
petitioner_arguments: The reliance placed upon by the trial Court, as well as the High Court on the confessional statement of the appellant made to the investigating officer PW-9 cannot stand.

The whole case is based on circumstantial evidence, therefore, our only endeavour is to find out whether the chain of circumstance noted by the trial Court, as well as the High Court was complete without any disruption in order to confirm the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant.
respondent_arguments: The trial Court, as well as the High Court have gathered the chain of circumstances, which led to the killing of the deceased by the appellant.
Since the chain of circumstances was complete in every respect, the conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant does not call for interference.
court_reasoning: The law on this aspect is quite clear, which we wish to explain at the very outset and before examining the chain of circumstances noted and explained in the judgment impugned.
A confession or an admission is evidence against the maker of it so long as its admissibility is not excluded by some provision of law.

The expression 'accused of any offence' in S. 25 would cover the case of an accused who has since been put on trial, whether or not at the time when he made the confessional statement, he was under arrest or in custody as an accused in that case or not.
holding: The conviction and sentence imposed on the appellant does not call for interference.

The admissible portion of the first information report Ex. P-42 must be excluded from evidence as the rest of the statement amounts to confession of committing the crime and is not admissible in evidence.
